CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain and redness of the right big toe for two weeks, worsening over the past week.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with a two-week history of right big toe pain that has been intermittent but became significantly worse last week during a trade show convention where he was unable to walk the halls. He describes the pain as throbbing in nature with occasional sharp, stabbing quality, especially with movement or prolonged walking. Patient reports walking on his heel to avoid bending the toe. Pain is exacerbated by light pressure, including from bed sheets at night. He denies a specific injury but notes onset of redness and warmth to the toe, which prompted him to seek care. He has tried ibuprofen 200 mg twice daily without significant relief. Notably, cycling does not aggravate symptoms as he pedals with the back of his feet. He typically wears flip-flops or regular shoes on regular pedals.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with any pressure or movement of the big toe joint, including passive range of motion. Pain worsens with plantar flexion of the toe. Patient notes a grinding sensation with medial-lateral movement of the joint. Denies stomach problems or history of gastrointestinal issues. Denies systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
None documented.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 200 mg twice daily (over-the-counter, for current toe pain).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is employed and works on his feet daily. He is an active individual who enjoys cycling (over 800 miles on trails last year) and fishing. He denies riding a bike but clarifies he is more of a runner. He enjoys spicy Mexican food.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Foot examination reveals redness of the right big toe. Range of motion testing of the first metatarsophalangeal joint shows approximately 10 degrees of plantar flexion with pain, worsening to 20 degrees. Dorsiflexion causes pain but less than with plantar flexion. Medial-lateral motion of the joint elicits pain with a grinding sensation. Palpation between the first and second toes causes mild discomfort. Palpation on the lateral (outside) aspect of the big toe joint causes significant pain. A small bone spur is palpated on the joint.

RESULTS
X-ray of the right foot reveals a large spur on the dorsal aspect of the first metatarsophalangeal joint with significant cartilage loss consistent with osteoarthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hallux rigidus (osteoarthritis of the first metatarsophalangeal joint) of the right foot with bone spur formation.

Plan:
1. Orthotic insert for shoe to reduce motion and pressure on the joint.
2. Meloxicam 1 tablet once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Patient counseled regarding potential gastrointestinal side effects, specifically heartburn or epigastric pain, and instructed to discontinue and call if these occur.
3. Continue regular work and activities to assess treatment efficacy.
4. Follow-up appointment in two weeks to assess response to conservative treatment.
5. If significant improvement not achieved, consider more invasive interventions including intra-articular injection or surgical options such as joint debridement or first metatarsophalangeal joint fusion.
